name: Coffee Pub Chameleon
tagline: One place for the whole group.
description: A private place for your group. Chat all week, call when it counts, and keep the plans, the maps and the notes right beside it. A space can be a trip, a campaign or a project.
pitch: Chat all week, call when it counts, and keep the plans, the maps and the notes right beside it. Yours, on your own address.

features.title: Chat and call
features.text: A chat that stays open between sessions, and a call with voice and video when you want one. Step into a side conversation and come back, or pop the call out into its own window.

areas.lead: A chat for your group, a call when you want one, and the tools you need beside them: the itinerary, the map, the dates and the budget. One address for your people, and nobody else's.

sections.title: A chat, and a call when you want one
sections.text: Chat for the whole trip, any day of the week. When talking is not enough, start a call with voice and video. Step into a side conversation and come back. Pop the call out into its own window. The chat is there whether or not you are on the call.

sections.title: An itinerary everyone can see
sections.text: In a trip, the Planner is called the Itinerary. It lays the trip out day by day: what you know, what your options are, what you have decided. Flights, stays, stops, ideas between days, and the cost of each.

sections.title: Money without the awkward bit
sections.text: Costs planned and paid, a target, and who owes whom. Add a cost from the itinerary and it is counted once.

sections.title: Dates and to-dos, together
sections.text: One calendar for the group, a month, a week or a list, with a to-do list beside it. Give a task a day and it lands on the calendar.

sections.title: Decide, then move on
sections.text: Ask the group: pick one, pick any, suggest another option. The result can carry straight onto the itinerary.

sections.title: What a trip comes with
sections.text: Each of these is a module. It can sit beside the chat, float over it or open in its own window. And more you can turn on, such as the Assistant, which answers questions about anything the group holds.

sections.title: In your pocket, too
sections.text: The same screens fit a phone, so the plan is there when you are in the street.

sections.title: A chat, and a call when you want one
sections.text: Chat for the whole campaign, any day of the week. When talking is not enough, start a call with voice and video. Take a few players into a whisper and come back. Pop the call out into its own window. The chat is there whether or not you are on the call. The Common room is where everyone in the group meets, whichever campaign they are in.

sections.title: A timeline everyone can see
sections.text: The Campaign planner lays the campaign out on a timeline, day by day. The recap of last session sits on its day, where the next game master or player will look for it.

sections.title: Every player on stream
sections.text: Each player is an OBS source on a clear background. Show their video, or a Character picture that stands in for them. Put your players on a stream, or over a map, with no editing.

sections.title: What a campaign comes with
sections.text: Each of these is a module. It can sit beside the chat, float over it or open in its own window. And more you can turn on, such as Places and Maps, for the world your players move through.

sections.title: In your pocket, too
sections.text: The same screens fit a phone, so the campaign is there when you are away from the table.

steps.title: Get an environment
steps.text: Its own address, its own sign-in, its own people. Nothing in it is shared with anyone else's.

steps.title: Make spaces in it
steps.text: A space is a place to meet: a chat, a call when you want one, and the modules you turn on for it. A family might have one, a company one per team, a game night one per campaign.

steps.title: Share a link
steps.text: Members sign in. Guests can come into a space with just a name, when you allow it.

stepsNote: The owner sets the name, the look, the people, the spaces and the modules. I run the servers, the call service, the updates and the backups. Or run the whole thing yourself: the same software can be self-hosted.

callout.title: Yours, and private
callout.text: No ads, and nobody selling what you say. Your people, plans and files live in your environment and are not shared with anyone else's. You can run it on your own server if you would rather.
